questions.question: When dropping off students at school, a driver should:

options.text: Turn off the engine to secure the bus.
Leave the key in the ignition when leaving the driver's seat.
Read a book while students get off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off the engine to secure the bus.
questions.explanation: When students get off at school, turn off the engine to secure the bus. Remove the key from the ignition if you leave the driver's seat. You must watch the students while they unload.

questions.question: Mirrors should be adjusted when driving a school bus:

options.text: While driving.
Before you start driving.
By the students.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before you start driving.
questions.explanation: Always check and adjust all mirrors before you start driving the school bus.

questions.question: Crossover mirrors help the driver see:

options.text: The danger zone in front of the bus.
The rear bumper.
The left side of the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: The danger zone in front of the bus.
questions.explanation: Crossover mirrors show the danger zone directly in front of the bus. They also show danger zones on the left and right sides of the bus, from the front to the service door.

questions.question: For a parallel parking maneuver, you should:

options.text: Back up past the space, then pull forward into it.
Pull forward past the space, then back into it.
Pull forward directly into the space.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull forward past the space, then back into it.
questions.explanation: Drive past the parking space on the right side. Then back into the space, getting the rear of your vehicle as close to the back of the space as possible. Your vehicle must be completely within the space boundaries.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing during the driving test, you should:

options.text: Pass another vehicle on the tracks if it is moving too slowly.
Change lanes while on the tracks.
Not change gears while on the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not change gears while on the tracks.
questions.explanation: While any part of your vehicle is on railroad tracks, do not stop, change gears, pass another vehicle, or change lanes.

questions.question: ABS helps a driver to:

options.text: Drive faster.
Keep control of the vehicle when braking.
See farther ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep control of the vehicle when braking.
questions.explanation: Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS) prevent the wheels from locking up and help you keep control of your vehicle when braking on slippery surfaces.

questions.question: During the basic control skills test, you get points if you:

options.text: Pull up once.
Check your position.
Cross over exercise boundaries.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cross over exercise boundaries.
questions.explanation: The examiner counts how many times your vehicle touches or crosses a boundary line. Each crossing counts as an error and points against your score.

questions.question: Pre-trip inspections should be done:

options.text: Differently each time to focus on different items.
The same way each time so you don't forget anything.
Once in a while.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same way each time so you don't forget anything.
questions.explanation: Do a pre-trip inspection the same way before every drive. This helps you learn all the steps and makes sure you don't skip anything.

questions.question: ABS allows you to:

options.text: Drive faster.
Drive less carefully.
Keep control on slippery roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep control on slippery roads.
questions.explanation: ABS prevents the wheels from locking up on slippery surfaces. If you brake hard on a slippery road, ABS helps you keep control. Drive and brake the same way with or without ABS.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing during the driving test, you should:

options.text: Pass another vehicle on the tracks if it is going too slow.
Get out and check for a train.
Not change gears while on the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not change gears while on the tracks.
questions.explanation: While any part of your vehicle is on railroad tracks, do not stop, change gears, pass another vehicle, or change lanes.

questions.question: When students board a school bus, the driver should:

options.text: Read a book.
Check all mirrors.
Only look at the students.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check all mirrors.
questions.explanation: Watch all mirrors while students board. Look for any students running to catch the bus.

questions.question: If a driver needs to leave a school bus to check on waiting students, the driver should:

options.text: Leave the bus running.
Turn the bus off and take the key.
Ask a student to watch the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the bus off and take the key.
questions.explanation: Always turn off the bus and take the key with you. Check around and under the bus for any missing students.

questions.question: Where is the overhead inside rearview mirror located?

options.text: Above the windshield on the driver's side of the bus.
Above the door across from the driver.
Above the emergency door in the rear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Above the windshield on the driver's side of the bus.
questions.explanation: The overhead inside rearview mirror is mounted above the windshield on the driver's side. It helps you watch students inside the bus.

questions.question: The overhead inside rearview mirror should show:

options.text: The rear tires.
All students on the bus.
The floor of the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: All students on the bus.
questions.explanation: Position the mirror to see all students, including those sitting directly behind the driver.

questions.question: If you are stopped at a railroad crossing while driving a school bus, you should:

options.text: Get ready to move as soon as a train passes.
Ignore signs and signals.
Open the door to listen for approaching trains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Open the door to listen for approaching trains.
questions.explanation: Do not rely only on signals. Tell students to be quiet, open the front door, and look and listen for trains. Check for trains from both directions before crossing the tracks.

questions.question: When approaching a school bus stop, the driver should:

options.text: Not use their mirrors.
Approach slowly and carefully.
Stop on the sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Approach slowly and carefully.
questions.explanation: Always approach bus stops slowly and carefully.

questions.question: If your bus has a roof-mounted strobe light, when should you use it?

options.text: When it is hard to see.
All the time.
Only at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it is hard to see.
questions.explanation: Use the strobe light when visibility is poor.

questions.question: After a trip, a post-trip inspection should include all of the following, except:

options.text: Looking for articles left on the bus.
Checking for sleeping students.
Opening windows.

questions.correctAnswerText: Opening windows.
questions.explanation: Check for sleeping students, belongings left behind, open windows or doors, mechanical problems, and damage.

questions.question: What is an inside rearview mirror used for?

options.text: Watch students inside the bus.
Inspect the outside of the bus.
See vehicles changing lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch students inside the bus.
questions.explanation: The overhead inside rearview mirror watches student activity. Adjust it to see all students, including those directly behind the driver.

questions.question: If students cause a disturbance while others are getting off the bus, what should you do?

options.text: Walk to the back of the bus right away to handle it while students unload.
Wait until all students finish unloading, then handle the disturbance.
Have a student close by deal with it while you watch the unloading.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until all students finish unloading, then handle the disturbance.
questions.explanation: Loading and unloading students requires your full attention. Handle behavior problems after all students have safely left the bus.
